content:
Stuck PRs — emergency alerts for wedged automation.

An hourly bot job (stuck-alerts.yml) posts here when a Tau Ceti pipeline gets stuck in a way it cannot recover from on its own: a last-known-good mathlib bump whose build stays red, a pin that has stopped advancing, a fully-green in-scope PR the merge path never merged, a Review stuck issue, a scheduled workflow that stopped firing, main gone red, or an unresolved mathlib incompatibility.

Treat every message here as "go fix an infrastructure bug", not "a human please hand-hold one PR". If something lands in this topic, the right response is to make the wedge impossible to recur — patch the script, workflow, guard, or pin — not to nudge one PR through by hand. Normal backlog (a PR awaiting its first review, changes nobody addressed, open roadmap issues) deliberately never appears here.

Each alert is a single message, edited to :check: when it clears; an ongoing one is never re-posted. The full catalogue and the reasoning live in scripts/zulip/stuck_alerts.py.
Do you expect discussion about a stuck PR to occur in this channel, or is it just for reporting stuck PRs?

I'm hoping that stuck PRs will be rare, and mostly represent breakages in the system that require a PR modifying the infrastructure.

In particular, I don't want "the contributor and the reviewers couldn't agree", to count as "stuck". Such PRs should just be closed after some time window.
